thread:
incident-bot: Incident detected: container restarts on prod-serving-7 due to GPU OOM during prefill. Auto-alerting on-call. (rule: prefill-gpu-oom > 5 restarts/5m)

incident-bot: Triggered automated mitigation: started temporary routing to fallback pool 'prod-hotpool-2' and increased eviction agressiveness.

sara_eng: seeing CPU/gpu metrics — prefill spike from long prompts (avg tokens 28k) starting ~03:02 UTC. Customers hitting 502s?

miguel_oncall: I'm on it. Confirming container restarts on node srv-gpu-17, docker restarts every ~22s. Pulling logs now.

anya_sre: tagging for pager handoff. miguel, can you try dropping PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS and disabling batching for new requests? Quick commands below:

anya_sre: ```
# reduce tolerated prefill length
kubectl -n serving set env deploy/llm-worker PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=8192
# temporary disable continuous batching
kubectl -n serving patch configmap runtime-config -p '{"data":{"batching.enabled":"false"}}'
```

miguel_oncall: applied PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=8192 and set batching.enabled=false. Restarting deployment slices to pick up config.

jordan_support: support queue updated: 2 customers reported 502s, one on EU region. Both mention big file->chat dump leading to long system prompt. Notifying CSMs.

miguel_oncall: logs show CUDA OOM: "out of memory when trying to allocate 1.2 GiB" during prefill KV allocation. kvcache eviction didn't trigger before crash.

anya_sre: enabling aggressive kvcache trim and fallback to quantized variant for new traffic. Command:

anya_sre: ```
# turn on kvcache aggressive trim
curl -X POST "https://ops-api.internal/runtime/kvcache/trim?policy=aggressive&scope=prod-serving"
# route new sessions under threshold to small-8-bit model
curl -X POST "https://ops-api.internal/routing/override" -d '{"match":"prefill_tokens>4096","route":"redwood-small-q8"}'
```

miguel_oncall: did kvcache trim, routing override accepted. Observing fewer restarts in the fallback pool. Node srv-gpu-17 still flapping, cordoned it.

ops-bot: Node srv-gpu-17 cordoned by miguel_oncall at 03:14 UTC. Evacuating pods.

incident-bot: Ongoing: 14 restarts in last 10m cluster prod-serving, tailing errors: CUDA OOM / container restart loop. Impact: degraded request success rate ~84% -> 96% after routing overrides.

sara_eng: good. Please push a short customer-facing note to the status page: mention degraded generation in EU for long prompts, mitigations in place, ETA ~1h while we stabilize.

jordan_support: drafted status update and posted: "We're experiencing degraded responses for long-context requests in EU. We're mitigating by routing long requests to lower-memory variants and applying server-side limits. We'll update in 1 hour."

miguel_oncall: follow-up mitigation: scaled down max_batch_size from 32 -> 8 for prod-serving to reduce peak mem pressure. Patch applied to runtime config.

anya_sre: started a live runbook check: verify no dirty GPU memory holds after restarts, confirm cuda-sanity hooks on the runtime. Miguel, can you collect a minidump from one crashed container?

miguel_oncall: grabbing minidump and nvprof traces now, uploading to /var/artifacts/6923456789.

incident-bot: Pager: assigned to miguel_oncall and anya_sre. Priority: P1.

sara_eng: next steps: follow up with model team to evaluate smaller quantized variants as default for >8k tokens, and update Optimize suggestions to detect customer prompts that may exceed safe prefill sizes.

jordan_support: CX notified. No escalations to legal required. CSMs pinged customers with temporary workaround (split upload into segments).

miguel_oncall: status 03:34 UTC — restarts dropped to 0 in prod-serving fallback pool, overall success back to 98%. Node srv-gpu-17 remains cordoned for deeper postmortem.

anya_sre: closing active mitigation loop. Creating incident ticket with timeline and artefacts: INC-6923456789. Please add any additional notes.

jordan_support: adding customer complaint IDs and CSM outreach notes to INC-6923456789.

incident-bot: Incident INC-6923456789 created. Postmortem requested within 72h.

sara_eng: thanks team :thumbsup: we'll run a regression test on prefill memory accounting and add a prefill backpressure guard to runtime.
